children.prompt: Simplify $1-\sin^2 x$, and hence find the value of $\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/3}\frac{2}{1-\sin^2 x}\,dx$.

answer.worked:
$$1-\sin^2 x=\cos^2 x$$
$$\begin{align*}\frac{2}{1-\sin^2 x}&=\frac{2}{\cos^2 x}\\&=2\sec^2 x\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\int_0^{\pi/3}\frac{2}{1-\sin^2 x}\,dx&=\int_0^{\pi/3}2\sec^2 x\,dx\\&=[2\tan x]_0^{\pi/3}\\&=2\tan\frac{\pi}{3}-2\tan0\\&=2\sqrt3\end{align*}$$

The inner function is $x^3$, with derivative $3x^2$. No constant adjustment is needed.

The inner function is $\cos x$, with derivative $-\sin x$.

answer.worked:
The denominator is $f(x)=x^2-9$, so $f'(x)=2x$. No adjustment is needed.
$$\begin{align*}\int\frac{2x}{x^2-9}\,dx&=\ln|x^2-9|+C\end{align*}$$

The denominator is $f(x)=3x^2+x$, so $f'(x)=6x+1$. No adjustment is needed.
$$\begin{align*}\int\frac{6x+1}{3x^2+x}\,dx&=\ln|3x^2+x|+C\end{align*}$$

The denominator is $f(x)=x^2+x-3$, so $f'(x)=2x+1$. No adjustment is needed.
$$\begin{align*}\int\frac{2x+1}{x^2+x-3}\,dx&=\ln|x^2+x-3|+C\end{align*}$$

The denominator is $f(x)=2+5x-3x^2$, so $f'(x)=5-6x$. No adjustment is needed.
$$\begin{align*}\int\frac{5-6x}{2+5x-3x^2}\,dx&=\ln|2+5x-3x^2|+C\end{align*}$$

The denominator is $f(x)=1+e^x$, so $f'(x)=e^x$. No adjustment is needed.
$$\begin{align*}\int\frac{e^x}{1+e^x}\,dx&=\ln(1+e^x)+C\end{align*}$$
Absolute value signs are unnecessary because $1+e^x>0$.

The denominator is $f(x)=1+e^{-x}$, so $f'(x)=-e^{-x}$.
$$\begin{align*}\int\frac{e^{-x}}{1+e^{-x}}\,dx&=-\int\frac{-e^{-x}}{1+e^{-x}}\,dx\\&=-\ln(1+e^{-x})+C\end{align*}$$
Absolute value signs are unnecessary because $1+e^{-x}>0$.

The denominator is $f(x)=e^x+e^{-x}$, so $f'(x)=e^x-e^{-x}$. No adjustment is needed.
$$\begin{align*}\int\frac{e^x-e^{-x}}{e^x+e^{-x}}\,dx&=\ln(e^x+e^{-x})+C\end{align*}$$
Absolute value signs are unnecessary because $e^x+e^{-x}>0$.

answer.worked:
The inner function is $x^2$, with derivative $2x$.
$$\begin{aligned}\int xe^{x^2}\,dx&=\frac12\int 2xe^{x^2}\,dx\\&=\frac12e^{x^2}+C.\end{aligned}$$

The inner function is $x^2-7$, with derivative $2x$.
$$\begin{aligned}\int 4xe^{x^2-7}\,dx&=2\int 2xe^{x^2-7}\,dx\\&=2e^{x^2-7}+C.\end{aligned}$$

The inner function is $3x^2+4x+1$, with derivative $6x+4=2(3x+2)$.
$$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int(3x+2)e^{3x^2+4x+1}\,dx\\&=\frac12\int(6x+4)e^{3x^2+4x+1}\,dx\\&=\frac12e^{3x^2+4x+1}+C.\end{aligned}$$

The inner function is $x^3-3x^2$, with derivative $3x^2-6x=3(x^2-2x)$.
$$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int(x^2-2x)e^{x^3-3x^2}\,dx\\&=\frac13\int(3x^2-6x)e^{x^3-3x^2}\,dx\\&=\frac13e^{x^3-3x^2}+C.\end{aligned}$$

The inner function is $x^{-1}$, with derivative $-x^{-2}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\int x^{-2}e^{x^{-1}}\,dx&=-\int(-x^{-2})e^{x^{-1}}\,dx\\&=-e^{x^{-1}}+C.\end{aligned}$$

The inner function is $-x\sqrt{x}=-x^{3/2}$, with derivative $-\frac32\sqrt{x}$.
$$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int-\sqrt{x}e^{-x\sqrt{x}}\,dx\\&=\frac23\int\left(-\frac32\sqrt{x}\right)e^{-x\sqrt{x}}\,dx\\&=\frac23e^{-x\sqrt{x}}+C.\end{aligned}$$

answer.worked:

$$\begin{align*}\int_0^k(e^{2x}-2e^x)\,dx&=\left[\frac12e^{2x}-2e^x\right]_0^k\\&=\frac12e^{2k}-2e^k+\frac32\end{align*}$$
Setting this equal to $\frac32$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac12e^{2k}-2e^k&=0\\e^k\left(\frac12e^k-2\right)&=0\end{align*}$$
Since $e^k>0$, $e^k=4$, so $k=\ln4$.

content.prompt:
It is known that
$$\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\ln x}{x}\right)=\frac{1-\ln x}{x^2}$$
(Do NOT prove this.)

$$\int\frac{1-\ln x}{x \ln x}dx$$

answer.worked:
Divide the numerator and denominator by $x^2$:
$$\int\frac{1-\ln x}{x\ln x}\,dx=\int\frac{\frac{1-\ln x}{x^2}}{\frac{\ln x}{x}}\,dx$$
This is $\int\frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}\,dx$ with $f(x)=\frac{\ln x}{x}$.
$$\begin{align*}&=\ln\left|\frac{\ln x}{x}\right|+C\\&=\ln|\ln x|-\ln|x|+C\end{align*}$$

content.prompt:
Without evaluating the integrals, which one of the following integrals is greater than zero?
(A) $\displaystyle\int_{-\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{x}{2+\cos x} \, dx$
(B) $\displaystyle\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} x^3 \sin x \, dx$
(C) $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^1 (e^{-x^2}-1) \, dx$
(D) $\displaystyle\int_{-2}^2 \tan^{-1}(x^3) \, dx$

answer.worked:
(A) $\frac{x}{2+\cos x}$ is odd, so its integral over a symmetric interval is $0$.
(B) $x^3\sin x$ is even and positive on $(0,\pi)$, so the integral is greater than $0$.
(C) $e^{-x^2}-1\le0$, so the integral is negative.
(D) $\tan^{-1}(x^3)$ is odd, so the integral is $0$.
The answer is (B).

Since $\cos x\ge0$ on $\left[0,\frac\pi2\right]$:
$$\begin{align*}&=\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos x(\sin x)^{1/2}\,dx\\&=\left[\frac23(\sin x)^{3/2}\right]_0^{\pi/2}\\&=\frac23\end{align*}$$

entries.description:
Because of the close relationship between primitives and the definite integral, we call the general primitive the indefinite integral. We write it using an integral sign without upper or lower limits.
For example:
\[\int x^2\,dx=\frac{x^3}{3}+C\]
A definite integral is a number that represents the area under a curve.
An indefinite integral is an expression that represents the general primitive function.
We call the process of finding the primitive integration and use the term ‘integral’ to refer to both the definite and indefinite integrals.
The expression being integrated is called the integrand.
